sources.title: Teaching computer programming with PRIMM: a sociocultural perspective
sources.access_level: selected full-text sections of 42-page manuscript: participant recruitment, assessments, results and limitations
sources.population: English secondary-school pupils aged 11–14 learning Python
sources.design: mixed-methods classroom comparison; volunteer teachers trained in PRIMM; usual school materials in controls; 8–12 weeks
sources.findings: PRIMM group had higher post-test scores; reported rank-test effect r=.13. Teacher interviews described practical benefits.
sources.limitations: Author-stated: volunteer teachers, insufficient demographic data, nonvalidated assessments, uncontrolled comparator lessons. Reviewer: teacher training/materials/dialogue form a bundle; no randomized Haskell or self-paced university test. Do not repeat the manuscript's interpretation of r=.13 as 13% variance explained.

sources.title: Reducing withdrawal and failure rates in introductory programming with subgoal labeled worked examples
sources.access_level: selected publisher full-text sections: Method, Participants, quiz/exam results
sources.population: university introductory Java students; five course sections
sources.design: semester classroom quasi-experiment comparing conventional versus subgoal-labeled worked examples
sources.findings: Better formative quiz performance, but no statistically significant improvement in average exam performance; lower exam variance and fewer withdrawals/failing exam averages reported.
sources.limitations: Section/instructor effects and selection remain possible; one control section online. Outcomes vary by measure. Earlier 2019 design and explanation-response papers reuse this project and are not independent replications.
sources.locations: Method; Participants; Exam performance; Withdrawal and failure

sources.title: From Studying Examples to Solving Problems: Fading Worked-Out Solution Steps Helps Learning
sources.access_level: selected full-text sections of six-page Cognitive Science Society proceedings paper
sources.population: German ninth-grade physics classes; Mississippi State psychology students learning probability
sources.design: classroom quasi-experiment; randomized laboratory fading versus example/problem pairs
sources.findings: Fading benefited near-transfer performance in both studies; neither showed a significant far-transfer benefit.
sources.limitations: Small samples and immediate domain-specific assessments; different fading directions across studies. Haskell benefit is inferred. Distinct from Renkl/Atkinson 2003 conceptual paper.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society

sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
sources.access_level: selected full-text Methods, Results and General Discussion; author-lab PDF
sources.design: two experiments: prose study/re-study versus free recall without feedback; immediate and delayed tests
sources.findings: Restudy favored five-minute performance; retrieval favored delayed retention. Experiment 2: repeated-testing group recalled 61% versus repeated-study 40% after one week.
sources.limitations: Prose idea-unit recall, not programming construction or type inference. Retrieval and study periods differed in duration; avoid claiming identical practice time in every condition. Not evidence that reading is dispensable.

sources.title: Spacing Effects in Learning: A Temporal Ridgeline of Optimal Retention
sources.access_level: selected full-text current-study, Methods, Discussion; university-hosted published PDF
sources.population: online adult memory panel; ages 18–72, mean 34
sources.design: random assignment to 26 gap/retention-interval combinations; 32 trivia facts; recall and recognition
sources.findings: Optimal review gap depended on retention interval; performance rose then fell with increasing gap. Approximate optimal ratios: 20–40% for one-week delay, 5–10% for one-year delay.
sources.limitations: Trivia retention and completer analysis; attrition increased at longer delays. Not a universal 10–20% schedule or demonstrated programming retention effect.

sources.title: Enhancing Syntax Error Messages Appears Ineffectual
sources.access_level: selected full-text Evaluation, Results and Discussion; university-hosted PDF
sources.population: University of Auckland accelerated summer CS1 students learning Java
sources.design: random allocation; 10 short CodeWrite method-body exercises over weeks 2–3; raw versus enhanced syntax messages
sources.findings: No significant benefit on consecutive noncompiling submissions, overall noncompiling attempts, or correction attempts for common error categories.
sources.limitations: Single short course, small tasks and specific enhancement style; no delayed conceptual assessment. Null result does not establish all enhancements ineffective.

sources.title: Effective compiler error message enhancement for novice programming students
sources.access_level: selected full-text author-uploaded original manuscript on ResearchGate; author-site accepted PDF redirected to suspended page
sources.population: first-semester Java CS1 students at one Irish institution
sources.design: successive-year control/intervention comparison; Decaf raw versus raw plus enhanced messages
sources.findings: Reduced error-frequency and several repeated-error measures under enhancement.
sources.limitations: Historical cohorts, no random allocation; compiler IDs approximate students, some duplication/other-tool use possible. Error frequency is not independent mastery. Similar error-rank distributions across languages do not prove equivalent instructional effects.
sources.discovered_by: Q06; expanded journal study search result; snowball P06

sources.title: Not the Silver Bullet: LLM-enhanced Programming Error Messages are Ineffective in Practice
sources.access_level: selected author full-text HTML: participants, procedure, results and limitations
sources.population: European university first-year CS students, second programming semester, C
sources.design: within-participant six-task debugging study; task-specific random assignment to GCC, handwritten or GPT-4 explanations
sources.findings: GPT-4 was faster than stock messages on only one task; handwritten explanations generally performed better. Preference for GPT-4 did not imply faster repair.
sources.limitations: Six selected bugs, timed repair, permitted web search; same researcher authored bugs and expert messages; GPT-4 also displayed stock messages. No delayed learning measure. Findings cannot establish current-model or Haskell effectiveness.

sources.title: Understanding Conceptual Transfer for Students Learning New Programming Languages
sources.access_level: selected author-uploaded full-text sections: participants, study procedures and results; institutional record has abstract only
sources.population: near-novice undergraduates Python→Java; IT masters students Java→Python
sources.design: two within-participant paper-based code-comprehension studies; categories of true, false and abstract true carryover
sources.findings: Syntax similarity accompanied positive or negative semantic transfer depending on whether meaning carried over; dissimilar syntax impeded recognition of shared concepts.
sources.limitations: Observational within-learner comparisons, selected concept categories and different test orders; not an intervention effect or imperative→Haskell result.

sources.title: Notional Machines and Introductory Programming Education
sources.access_level: selected author-uploaded full-text introduction and conceptual discussion; institutional metadata verified
sources.design: narrative/conceptual review, not a new intervention experiment
sources.findings: Proposes making the program-execution model an explicit learning objective and relates this to mental models and programming difficulties.
sources.limitations: Framework evidence, not an effect estimate; no new N. A Haskell notional machine must respect non-strict evaluation rather than importing imperative state/line-order semantics.

sources.title: Students’ ways of experiencing visual program simulation
sources.access_level: abstract and institutional metadata only; attempted publisher full-text open failed
sources.population: novice programmers; precise course/language not verified
sources.findings: Six ways of experiencing simulation reported; some learners failed to attach meaning to visuals or connect them to programming practice.
sources.limitations: Abstract-only extraction: no verified N, interview protocol, sampling or coding details. Evidence of differing interpretations, not a causal visualization benefit or prevalence estimate.

sources.title: Counting days is a spacing incentive that unlocks the potential of low GPA students
sources.access_level: selected publisher full-text Methods, Results and Discussion
sources.population: university introductory Python; high-school/college Java courses
sources.design: individual RCT rewarding practice days versus question counts; instructor-cluster RCT of same incentive
sources.findings: Day incentives increased practice days. Within-course exam gains particularly benefited lower-GPA students; second experiment measured practice behavior, not comparable learning outcomes.
sources.limitations: Postrandomization exclusions, modeled GPA interaction; same adaptive/interleaving tool in both arms. Incentive effect is not pure spacing mediation causality; similar practice/assessment question types and one-course learning result limit transfer.
sources.discovered_by: Q25 result; citation trail from 2019 retrieval-tool paper; Q32
